To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the localism of action in community energy projects has the potential of scaling up to localism in policy and practice.
(1) Localism is a constraint in the process of community energy project development; (2) Localism is not a constraint in the community energy project development.

(i) Localism is a constraint to development due to localism and centralism of action, (ii) localism is a potential for development due to its ability to scale-up operations and (iii) the prospects of localism in development are contingent upon the nature of the localism of action.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prospects of localism and how it can be used as a tool for community empowerment and sustainable development.
how localism can be a useful tool in community energy access projects in Nigeria.
the prospects of localism in sustainable energy projects and how it can be used to address energy poverty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
localism is a constraint and an enabler for community energy projects in rural areas in Nigeria and other developing countries.
the prospects for localism in community renewable energy projects is a function of its conceptualisation and the power relations that shape its trajectory.
localism in the context of community energy projects is a good concept but it is not a panacea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

community-based renewable energy projects have the potential for scaling-up, and this would require a paradigm shift in how localism is conceptualised and implemented in development projects in Africa.
localism is not a panacea but it is a useful tool for community energy development in the developing world.
community energy projects in developing countries can be scaled-up to achieve a more sustainable development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local is the best site for knowledge and innovation in the energy transition process.
the localisation of energy projects is a necessary condition to ensure that the projects are sustainable and meet local needs and expectations.
localism is a powerful tool in the hands of local actors and can be used to influence the state in policy and project implementation.
